evidence_tier: REAL. Ablation C on claims: n_cal in {250, 1000, 4000} crossed with beta in {0, 3, 6}, 500 trials per cell. Produces the certifiable-shift-vs-budget table (definition of done, item 5).
question: What does the calibration budget buy? The theorem holds at any n_cal; the table prices dispersion and conservatism against budget and shift.

predictions.PC1: Oracle consistent at all nine cells. Its conservatism grows as the budget falls: oracle mean risk at n_cal = 250 is at least 0.005 below its n_cal = 4000 value at every beta (the B/(n+1) charge, 0.004 vs 0.00025, plus coarser plateau overshoot).
predictions.PC2: Weighted-arm trial dispersion scales like the square root of the budget: the ratio of the oracle's 90% spread (p95 - p05) between n_cal = 250 and n_cal = 4000 lies in [2.8, 5.7] at every beta (the 16x budget ratio predicts 4x, window allows 1.4x slack either way).
predictions.PC3: The table's headline: at n_cal = 250, beta = 6 (chi2 3.54, oracle ESS near 58 of 250), the oracle's p95 realized risk is at least 0.125 even though its mean is controlled; at n_cal = 4000, beta = 6, p95 is at most 0.115. A mean certificate at small budget under large shift is real but practically loose.
predictions.PC4: Estimated equivalence holds at every n_cal >= 1000 cell; at n_cal = 250 the equivalence CI may fail by width alone, and the paired-difference point estimate stays inside [-0.005, +0.005] at all nine cells.
predictions.PC5: Unweighted decays identically across budgets (its failure is bias, not variance): its mean risk at beta = 6 differs by at most 0.005 across the three budgets.

falsifiers.PC1: Oracle inconsistency anywhere follows the standing bug-presumption path; conservatism NOT growing as budget falls would mean the plateau overshoot dominates in the opposite direction and the B/(n+1) story is wrong here.
falsifiers.PC2: Scaling far off square root implicates ESS nonlinearity in threshold noise; report the measured exponent.
falsifiers.PC4: A paired-difference point estimate outside the margin at n_cal = 250 would mean small calibration samples interact with estimated weights beyond noise; that becomes a WP2 finite-sample term.
falsifiers.PC5: Budget-dependence of the unweighted arm would mean the finite-sample terms are not negligible even for the biased baseline; recheck before quoting any decay number at n_cal = 250.

decision_rule: Per-cell three-outcome rule at raw z = 1.645 (nine cells, exploratory labels) with named claims PC1-PC5 judged at the stated tolerances; equivalence at the 90% paired CI. Endpoints and rung labelling as standard.
notes: No design-phase probe was run; the PC3 bounds are derived from wp1c's measured trial dispersion at n_cal = 1000 scaled by the square-root law that PC2 itself tests, so a PC2 failure automatically requalifies PC3's derivation (this coupling is registered deliberately).

verdicts.PC1: PARTIAL. Oracle consistent 9/9. The conservatism gap between n_cal 250 and 4000 meets the registered 0.005 floor only at beta 6 (0.0081); at beta 0 and 3 the direction is right but the magnitude is 0.0015 and 0.0031. Verbatim: the B/(n+1)-plus-plateau charge grows with shift (weighted plateaus coarsen faster than unweighted ones), which the flat-floor prediction missed.
verdicts.PC2: MISS, verbatim and diagnostic: the 90% spread ratio between budgets 250 and 4000 is 1.75 / 2.06 / 2.42 at beta 0 / 3 / 6, all far below the registered [2.8, 5.7] square-root window; measured scaling exponent ~0.32 at beta 6 and lower at smaller shift. Cause identified: realized risk per trial is measured on a 1000-case evaluation window whose binomial noise (90% spread ~0.031) does not scale with n_cal and floors the dispersion. Calibration budget buys threshold precision; it cannot buy away deployment-window noise. This is the budget table's true headline.
verdicts.PC3: AUTO-REQUALIFIED per the registered coupling with PC2, and split: p95 at n_cal 250, beta 6 is 0.1440 (>= 0.125 as registered); at 4000 it is 0.1190 (> the registered 0.115 ceiling, by the same evaluation-noise floor PC2 identified).
verdicts.PC4: CONFIRMED, stronger than registered: equivalence holds at ALL nine cells including n_cal = 250 (largest paired diff +0.0037).
verdicts.PC5: CONFIRMED: unweighted at beta 6 spans 0.1212 to 0.1241 across budgets (max spread 0.0029 <= 0.005).
verdicts.table_note: The certifiable-shift-vs-budget table (definition of done, item 5) reads: mean control holds at every budget-shift cell for the weighted arms; what the budget buys at large shift is the conservatism margin (mean 0.088 at 250 vs 0.096 at 4000, beta 6) and roughly a 2.4x reduction in trial dispersion, floored by evaluation-window noise that no calibration budget removes.
